'''Oliver Lafayette''' (born May 6, 1984) is an American-born Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=2}}, he played at the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. A two-time [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] winner, Lafayette has also won the national championships in [[Greek Basket League|Greece]] and [[Lithuanian Basketball League|Lithuania]].

==High school and college career==
Lafayette attended Capitol High School in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]] and led the basketball team to a 29–3 record his senior year. Lafayette attended first [[Blinn College]] and [[Brown Mackie College]] before transferring to the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|University of Houston]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Matthew Aguilar |title=Seeing red – Defense is name of Lafayette's game |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98097272/seeing-red-defense-is-name-of-lafayett/ |access-date=21 March 2022 |work=[[El Paso Times]] |date=23 February 2006 |page=44|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> At Houston during his junior year, Lafayette started 30 of 31 games and earned 2nd team all Conference USA while finishing third in scoring in C-USA with a 15.7 points per game average. During his senior year in 2006–07, Lafayette averaged 14.3 points, 5.9 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. He also majored in sociology.<ref>[http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lafayette_oliver00.html Oliver Lafayette Player Bio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029132746/http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lafayette_oliver00.html |date=2014-10-29 }} UH Cougars</ref>

==Professional career==
[[File:Lafayette amb la premsa.ogv|thumb|230px|right|Lafayette talks to Press in his presentation as a [[Valencia BC]] player.]]
Lafayette played with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] during the 2009–10 season in the [[NBA Development League]]. With the Mad Ants, the guard started 42 of 48 games and averaged 17.1 points, 6.5 assists and 1.8 steals in 35.3 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Chris Forsberg |title=Another roster addition: Oliver Lafayette |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4673412/another-roster-addition-oliver-lafayette |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=13 April 2010}}</ref> On April 14, 2010, Lafayette signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]]<ref>{{cite news |author1=Julian Benbow |title=Bradley gets quicker fixer-upper |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98097745/bradley-gets-quicker-fixer-upper/ |access-date=21 March 2022 |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |date=3 July 2010 |page=C2}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Chris Forsberg |title=Lafayette looking to secure spot |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/columns/story?columnist=forsberg_chris&id=5358100 |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=6 July 2010}}</ref> and appeared in one game with the team in which he scored 7 points. Upon playing with the Celtics, Lafayette became the 23rd former Houston Cougar to play in the NBA.<ref>[http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041510aaa.html Former Guard Oliver Lafayette Makes NBA Debut with Celtics on Wednesday] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131221015519/http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041510aaa.html |date=2013-12-21 }} uhcougars.com, April 15, 2010</ref>

On October 13, 2010, Lafayette signed with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] in Serbia,<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/76777/180/partizan-mt-s-grabs-lafayette-at-point-guard Partizan Mt:s grabs Lafayette at point guard]</ref> but the contract was terminated in November.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/79345/180/partizan-lafayette-out-jerrells-in Partizan: Lafayette out, Jerrells in]</ref>

In December 2010, Lafayette practiced with the Fort Wayne Mad Ants, his former team. He was going to sign with the Mad Ants once he was officially released from Partizan Belgrade.<ref>[http://www.news-sentinel.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20101215/SPORTS/12150321 Lafayette to return to Mad Ants roster] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120311073631/http://www.news-sentinel.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20101215/SPORTS/12150321 |date=March 11, 2012 }} news-sentinel.com, December 15, 2010</ref> After averaging 16.4 points per game with the Mad Ants, he signed a four-month contract with the Turkish team [[Beşiktaş Milangaz|Beşiktaş]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/21865/besiktas_sign_oliver_lafayette.html Besiktas sign Oliver LaFayette]</ref> But due to health problems, his contract was dropped.<ref>[http://www.cnnturk.com/2011/spor/basketbol/02/05/besiktas.cola.turkada.sok.gelisme/605813.0/ Beşiktaş Cola Turka'da şok gelişme]</ref>

In February 2011, Lafayette signed with [[Maccabi Ashdod B.C.|Maccabi Ashdod]] in Israel.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/israel/23365/maccabi_ashdod_tabs_oliver_lafayette.html Maccabi Ashdod tabs Oliver LaFayette]</ref> On October 5, 2011, he signed a one-year contract with [[Asseco Prokom Gdynia]] in Poland.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/poland/31529/asseco_prokom_gdynia_lands_oliver_lafayette.html Asseco Prokom Gdynia lands Oliver Lafayette]</ref>

In January 2012, Lafayette signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes Istanbul]] for the remainder of the 2011–12 season.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/92566/180/anadolu-efes-tabs-lafayette Anadolu Efes tabs Lafayette]</ref> Later that year, he joined [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/99168/7224/zalgiris-adds-lafayette-brings-back-juskevicius ZALGIRIS adds Lafayette, brings back Juskevicius]</ref> He signed with [[Valencia BC|Valencia Basket]] in the offseason in 2013.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130715071944/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/114859/8174 VALENCIA BASKET lands Lafayette]</ref>

On June 22, 2014, he signed a two-year deal with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Olympiacos announces Oliver Lafayette|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/123727/olympiacos-announces-oliver-lafayette.html|access-date=June 22, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=June 22, 2014}}</ref> On June 29, 2015, he parted ways with Olympiacos.<ref>{{cite news|title=Olympiakos and Oliver Lafayette parted ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/166105/olympiakos-and-oliver-lafayette-parted-ways.html|access-date=29 June 2015|work=sportando.com|date=29 June 2015}}</ref>

On July 9, 2015, he signed with the Italian club [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milano]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Un altro playmaker all'Olimpia: Oliver Lafayette|url=http://www.olimpiamilano.com/un-altro-playmaker-allolimpia-oliver-lafayette/|access-date=July 9, 2015|work=Olimpiamilano.com|date=July 9, 2015|language=it|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304165147/http://www.olimpiamilano.com/un-altro-playmaker-allolimpia-oliver-lafayette/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 18, 2016, Lafayette signed with Spanish team [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unicajabaloncesto.com/noticia-10057-lafayette-es-jugador-unicaja.html|title=Lafayette ya es jugador del Unicaja|publisher=unicajabaloncesto.com|language=es|date=18 July 2016|access-date=18 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/74yk7cdhmq3xecx3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821152812/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/74yk7cdhmq3xecx3|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 21, 2016|title=Unicaja adds point guard Lafayette|publisher=eurocupbasketball.com|date=18 July 2016|access-date=18 July 2016}}</ref> In April 2017, Lafayette won his second [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] with Unicaja after beating [[Valencia BC]] in the [[2017 EuroCup Finals|Finals]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/|title=7DAYS EuroCup Finals, Game 3: Unicaja Malaga is the champion!|date=5 April 2017|access-date=6 April 2017|publisher=Eurocupbasketball.com}}</ref>

On July 31, 2017, Lafayette signed with Italian club [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/242957/virtus-bologna-signs-oliver-lafayette.html Virtus Bologna signs Oliver Lafayette]</ref>

On November 13, 2018, Lafayette signed with Bosnian club [[KK Igokea|Igokea]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Igokea officially adds Oliver Lafayette |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/igokea-officially-adds-oliver-lafayette/ |work=Sportando |date=13 November 2018 |archive-date=February 15, 2020 |access-date=November 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215091300/https://sportando.basketball/en/igokea-officially-adds-oliver-lafayette/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==International career==
The [[Croatian Basketball Federation]] asked for permission to give Oliver Lafayette a Croatian citizenship for sports interest, which the [[Croatian Olympic Committee]] approved. Lafayette was awarded with a Croatian passport and represented [[Croatia national basketball team|Croatia]] at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Croatian Olympic Committee – News|url=http://www.hoo.hr/3353-v-matic-rados-i-golec-novi-kandidati-za-rio-2016.aspx|access-date=June 26, 2014|work=HOO.hr|date=June 26, 2014}}</ref>

==Overseas Elite==
In the summer of 2017, Lafayette joined two-time [[The Basketball Tournament]] defending champion [[Overseas Elite]]. On August 3, 2017, Blair's team, Overseas Elite won its third straight The Basketball Tournament championship with an 86–83 victory over Team Challenge ALS on ESPN.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thetournament.com/news/overseas-elite-completes-3-peat-defeat-team-challenge-als-86-83|title=OVERSEAS ELITE COMPLETES THE 3-PEAT, DEFEAT TEAM CHALLENGE ALS 86–83|date=August 4, 2017|access-date=August 10, 2017|archive-date=August 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810210720/http://thetournament.com/news/overseas-elite-completes-3-peat-defeat-team-challenge-als-86-83|url-status=dead}}</ref>
